definition: Mistral AI SAS (French: [mistʁal]) is a French artificial intelligence (AI) company headquartered in Paris.
details: Founded in 2023, it develops large language models (LLMs). As of 2025, the company has a valuation of more than US$14 billion, the highest among European AI companies. As of August 2026, its largest public model is Mistral Large 3, released in December 2025, a mixture of experts model with 675 billion parameters, of which 41 are active. Mistral released Le Chat, its chatbot, in February 2024, renamed to Mistral Vibe in 2026. Mistral is a primary beneficiary of a push by the European Union and its member governments towards digital sovereignty in response to the AI boom and AI arms race between the US and China. In September 2025, ASML, Europe's largest tech company and supplier of the semiconductor industry, invested €1.3 billion in Mistral, corresponding to an 11% shareholding.

explainer.lead: Mistral AI is a Paris-based company founded in 2023 that builds large language models, and it is the most valuable AI company in Europe. Its models matter as a European alternative in a field dominated by US and Chinese labs.

tiers.eli5: It's a French company that builds AI brains, kind of like a European rival to the big American AI makers.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick Mistral models when they want strong open or hosted LLMs with EU data-residency appeal; a pitfall is that model names and lineups change fast, so pin exact versions in production.
tiers.paperLevel: Its largest public model as of August 2026 is Mistral Large 3 (December 2025), a mixture-of-experts model with 675 billion total parameters, of which 41 billion are active per token.

explainer.example: A European bank wanting an LLM vendor under EU jurisdiction could deploy Mistral Large 3 and rely on only 41B of its 675B parameters being computed per token.
